# Claims and evidence ledger

This is the canonical list of what we know, what we think we know, and what we
do not know. Other researchers and agents should use these IDs when referring
to a finding, disputing it, or extending it.

## Status labels
| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **VERIFIED** | Reproduced directly from the sample bytes with a script; another person can re-run the check. |
| **OBSERVED** | Seen in the data, but the interpretation is not proven. |
| **HYPOTHESIS** | A plausible explanation that fits current evidence but has not been confirmed. |
| **UNKNOWN** | No reliable answer yet. |

Confidence: **H** = high, **M** = medium, **L** = low.

When a claim changes status, update this file and note the evidence in the
commit message. Do not silently promote a hypothesis to a fact.

Evidence should cite the relevant `docs/experiments/EXP-...` record and/or a
`tools/` command. The experiment log is append-only; if a result is corrected,
add a new experiment and mark `Supersedes` / `Superseded by`.

## Card / image
| ID | Claim | Status | Confidence | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-001 | The EU 2011 image is 8,057,257,984 bytes with SHA-256 `105e2032…76307`. | VERIFIED | H | `sha256sum`, `stat` |
| C-002 | It has an MBR with exactly one partition, type `0x0b`, start LBA 204802. | VERIFIED | H | `fdisk -l`, `7z l`, MBR bytes at `0x1be` |
| C-003 | The FAT32 volume label is `QSD-309-101`; cluster size 65,536 bytes. | VERIFIED | H | FAT boot sector, `7z l` |
| C-004 | The filesystem contains 39 directories, 480 files, 5,173,965,667 bytes. | VERIFIED | H | `7z x`, `find`, `du` |
| C-005 | `VER_INFO/HDD_INFO.TXT` contains six CRLF-separated lines: `QSD-302-100`, `QSD-309-101`, `02-110100-00`, `SDC08-EVEUR`, `11-05`, `470323501005`. | VERIFIED | H | hexdump of the 72-byte file |
| C-006 | The 100 MB before the FAT partition contains Clarion records (`CLARION ID` at `0x200`) and a firmware container at `0x200000`. | VERIFIED | H | raw bytes, see [firmware.md](../format/firmware.md) |
| C-007 | The 402,652,160-byte post-partition tail is almost entirely non-zero (400,365,370 bytes). | VERIFIED | H | byte scan |
| C-008 | The purpose of the post-partition tail is unknown. | UNKNOWN | — | no successful parser yet |
| C-009 | The map validity/activation mechanism (checksum, signature, CID binding, version code) is unknown. | UNKNOWN | — | no matching code or test yet |

## Common file header
| ID | Claim | Status | Confidence | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-010 | Most map files start with a 512-byte header containing the UTF-16**BE** strings `CLARION`, `HITACHI`, `CLA-NAVI05-01`, `FORMAT VERSION X08-02-00`, `DATA VERSION 11/06/27/01`, `V05.00.00`. | VERIFIED | H | hexdump of `MMAIN001.DAT`, `MAPAL001/*.DAT`, `RDSTM001.DAT`, `BICON001.DAT`, decompressed `REFER001` payloads |
| C-011 | The header contains a file-type-specific binary descriptor at `0x180`. | VERIFIED | H | identical prefix `ff ff 24 ff 12 c0 05 00 fb 50 0f f0`, then per-type bytes |
| C-012 | The meaning of the descriptor fields is unknown. | UNKNOWN | — | not decoded |
| C-013 | `DRSTR001.DAT` does not use this 512-byte header. | VERIFIED | H | first bytes are a 32-bit count + binary records |

## `.cmp` / `.ind`
| ID | Claim | Status | Confidence | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-020 | `.ind` is little-endian: `u32 uncompressed_size, u32 compressed_size, u32 chunk_count, u32 chunk_size, u32 chunk_offset[chunk_count]`. | VERIFIED | H | matches all 194 pairs; see [cmp-ind.md](../format/cmp-ind.md) |
| C-021 | `ind_size == 16 + 4 * chunk_count`. | VERIFIED | H | 194/194 |
| C-022 | `chunk_size` is `0x10000` (65,536) in every examined file. | VERIFIED | H | 194/194 |
| C-023 | Each chunk is an independent zlib stream; concatenating decompressed chunks yields exactly `uncompressed_size` bytes. | VERIFIED | H | 194/194, `tools/cmpind.py verify` |
| C-024 | Naive `zlib.decompress()` on the whole `.cmp` only returns the first stream and silently truncates large files. | VERIFIED | H | `ADDRE001`: 65,536 of 79,360 bytes |
| C-025 | The decompressed payload still starts with the 512-byte header. | VERIFIED | H | `COORD001` decompressed size 4,608 = 512 + 4,096 |
| C-026 | The record format inside address/POI payloads is not decoded. | UNKNOWN | — | only strings such as `STREET`, `area code`, `street name`, `dndc-id` observed |

## `DRSTR001.DAT`
| ID | Claim | Status | Confidence | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-030 | `DRSTR001.DAT` has **no header**. The node table starts at `0x0000` with the root node `/`; the 2011 sample has 40 nodes. `0x2f` is the ASCII `/` of the root name, not a count. | VERIFIED | H | EXP-2026-11-05-01; `40*40 + 324*32 = 11968` |
| C-031 | Node records are 40 bytes, name-first: `name[8]` at `+0x00`, `next_index` at `+0x14`, `parent_index+1` at `+0x16`, `entry_count` at `+0x18`, `listing_offset` at `+0x24`. | VERIFIED | H | 40/40 parse; invariants pass |
| C-032 | Listings are 32-byte entries: `name[13]` at `+0x00`, `type` at `+0x16` (0 = file, 2 = dir), `value` at `+0x1c`. | VERIFIED | H | 324 entries; names match FAT |
| C-033 | An earlier "one-node shift" was a parsing artefact: the table starts at `0x0000`, not `0x28`, and each node describes its own listing. | VERIFIED | H | corrected `tools/drstr.py`; listings tile exactly to EOF |
| C-034 | `next_index` is always `index + 1`; its purpose is unknown. | OBSERVED | H | all 40 nodes |
| C-035 | `CMP.LST` contains exactly `\SystemSD\REFER001\` (19 bytes, no newline). | VERIFIED | H | hexdump |
| C-036 | Entry `value`: for `.cmp` files it is the logical uncompressed size (`.ind`, 194/194); for `MAPAL001` tiles it is the **on-disk** size; for directories it is the recursive subtree total (verified for all 39 dirs). | VERIFIED | H | size invariants + FAT cross-check |
| C-037 | `MMAIN001.DAT` is **not** a manifest: no file names, offsets or checksums. It is a format/version descriptor (common header, per-language code list at `0x18c`, 3-section descriptor at `0x1ac`). | VERIFIED (negative) | H | full-byte analysis; CRC/Adler/sum probes negative |
| C-038 | There is no checksum/signature file on the card and no checksum field in `DRSTR001.DAT` or `MMAIN001.DAT`. Integrity of `REFER001` is zlib Adler-32 per 64 KiB chunk. | VERIFIED | H | 194/194 decompressions; field accounting |
| C-039 | The fixed data before the payload may extend to `0x5d6`, not 512 bytes: the 10-byte sequence `80 00 00 00 05 00 fb 50 0b 0b` appears at `0x5cc` in many files. | OBSERVED | M | cross-file hexdump; parser boundary not proven |

`jsr` site (matched by instruction stream alone) reading the callee literal at
the same instruction index. `--leaf` forces the path; a `DIFFERENT` leaf names
the first differing instruction and pool value.

## How to verify
Every active claim names an `EXP-...` record; this table gives the exact
repo command where one exists. `<img>` is a raw SD image (vendor data, kept
outside the repo), `<root>` an extracted card root, `<tile>` a `BxxRyyR.DAT`.

| Active claims | Command | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C-543–C-547, C-553, C-555, C-557, C-560–C-563 | `python3 tools/selftest.py` (or `--only <tool>`) | every `tool:*` suite `PASS`; `selftest: OK` |

| C-070–C-084, C-120–C-126, C-509–C-514 | no local command: external teardown/upstream sources only | see `sources.md`/`feedback-loop.md`; not reproduced here |
| C-110–C-116, C-132–C-142, C-150–C-156, C-210–C-216 | helpers `coord.py`/`poipoint.py`/`decode.py` are **not in `tools/`**; use `l2check.py` as the regression gate | original method in the named EXP |

## How to use this ledger
- When you verify or refute a claim, update its row and add the command/output
  to the evidence column.
- When you add a new claim, give it the next free ID in its section.
- Keep `docs/format/*.md` consistent with this file; the ledger wins if they
  disagree.
- Do not promote `OBSERVED`/`HYPOTHESIS` to `VERIFIED` without a reproducible
  check that another agent can run.

Geometry printed by `data_sectors=14743768 spc=128 count=115185 last=115186 first_past=115187 FAT=115200 phantom=13 (115187..115199)`. | VERIFIED (tool change, real image) | H | EXP-2026-11-19-M5.30-one-variable-card §1; `python3 tools/imgpatch.py --selftest` |

## M1.29 — `fn_audit`: a documented correction is `CORRECTED`, not `INSIDE` (C-3790–C-3799)
Extends M1.25. A `ctx` citation (a bare VA on a correction-marker line) is
`CORRECTED` — not a failure — only when the line itself resolves it; a live
`fn 0x…`/`sub_…`/target/const label of the same VA is never corrected, so the
verdict is per citation. `--fix-list` and the exit code follow `is_failure`.

| ID | Claim | Status | Confidence | Evidence |

The pair attaches only to the VA it names, so a repeated bare VA on the same line that matches no pair stays unresolved (M1.25 feedback rule). A pair naming a different start stays `INSIDE`; a cross-build map (`0x0041c7dc→0x00444540`) is a pair shape and not a correction. | VERIFIED (tool) | H | EXP-2026-11-15-M1.29-fn-audit; `python3 tools/fn_audit.py --selftest` (pair/wrong-start/cross-build/repeated-VA checks) |

## M1.30 — `fn_audit` frozen corpus snapshot (C-3860–C-3869)
`tools/fn_audit.py` can freeze its `--scope docs` corpus to one committed,
vendor-free JSON snapshot (`--write-snapshot`) and audit it against the image
plus a live scan (`--corpus`). The frozen part is the row identity
(`file/line/va/kind`, and a `ctx` row's paired `correction`); the stored
`class` is re-derived from `.pdata` every run, so a hand-edited class fails and
a months-old snapshot cannot pass.

| ID | Claim | Status | Confidence | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-3860 | On `archive/head256.img` (`92aa525d…`) the live `--scope docs` corpus is 17 files, 313 citations, 112 unique VAs, `START 229, INSIDE 0, CORRECTED 23, GAP 29 (leaf 29), AMBIGUOUS 0, UNMAPPED 32`, exit 0, empty `--fix-list`; `TODO.md` + 13 `docs/format/*.md` + `targets.json` + `chunk_decoder_l3.py` + `point_walk_l3.py`. | VERIFIED (tool) | H | EXP-2026-11-16-M1.30-fn-audit-snapshot; `python3 tools/fn_audit.py archive/head256.img --scope docs --quiet`, `python3 tools/fn_audit.py archive/head256.img --fix-list` |
| C-3861 | `--write-snapshot PATH` writes one row per citation (`file,line,va,kind,class,true_start,class_sha256`, sorted by `file:line:va`; `GAP` rows add `leaf`, `AMBIGUOUS` rows add candidates, `ctx` rows keep their paired `correction`) plus the exact summary and the image SHA-256, no image bytes. The committed `docs/research/fn-audit-corpus-2026-11-16.json` has 313 rows and SHA-256 `ddd113f84228ff85af85fb633beba8dd70ed5dc072b52a542af1511ee0102a1a` (H69 refreshed the pre-H69 `4606aa2a…`; a fresh `--write-snapshot` today differs only in moved line numbers, `9afe3f7d…`); two consecutive writes are byte-identical. | VERIFIED (tool) | H | EXP-2026-11-16-M1.30-fn-audit-snapshot; `python3 tools/fn_audit.py archive/head256.img --scope docs --write-snapshot /tmp/opencode/snap.json`, `sha256sum /tmp/opencode/snap.json`, two writes `cmp`-identical |

On the committed snapshot with `archive/head256.img` it prints the same summary as the live run and exits 0. | VERIFIED (tool) | H | EXP-2026-11-16-M1.30-fn-audit-snapshot; `python3 tools/fn_audit.py archive/head256.img --corpus docs/research/fn-audit-corpus-2026-11-16.json --quiet` |

## M1.26 — `fn_audit --scope l3` standing gate (C-3660–C-3669)
`tools/fn_audit.py --scope l3` widens the audit to the corpora the M9/M3 board

## H69 — snapshot refresh owner and moved-only warn policy (C-3900–C-3909)
`tools/fn_audit.py` splits live drift against the frozen corpus into
`CORPUS DRIFT` (same `(file,va,kind,class)` identity set, only `line` moved:
warn, exit 0) and `CORPUS STALE` (`new`/`gone`/verdict change: exit 1). The

## M1.31 — `pdata` leaf census: `rts` presence, no-`rts` stubs and the `0x400` cap (C-3960–C-3969)
`tools/pdata.py leaves --called {records,gaps,all}` classifies every `.pdata`
GAP of one module using the *uncapped* natural bound (next pdata START / next
call target / code end) and the first `rts` inside it: `complete`, `truncated`
(natural bound `> cap` and `rts` at/after the cap) or `stub` (no `rts`).
`fn_match._leaf_verdict` reports `TRUNCATED` for a cap-limited window that
misses the gap's natural bound and holds no `rts`, instead of a false `NOMATCH`.

## M5.45 — Tile-writer idempotence (C-4460–C-4469)
| ID | Claim | Status | Confidence | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-4460 | `tilewriter.splice_factory` is idempotent for a repeated identical splice. Its block decision is now three-way: **unchanged** when the rebuilt block equals the block already at the slot's tag (new branch; the block gets no write, the slot body is still written), **in place** when the slot owns its block and the new block fits, **append** otherwise. On EU 2011 `B48R058R` a full level-1 directory `(76,940)` splice of 1,024 parcels from the factory tile reports `appended=32`, `in_place=0`, `unchanged=0`, `superseded_bytes=1,789,864`; the same input spliced over the output, twice in a row, reports `appended=0`, `unchanged=32`, `superseded_bytes=0` and is byte-identical to the first output (`sha256 b746427cb056…34c2ef`), so the append is once per changed block, not once per run. Before the branch the repeat took the in-place path (32 writes to the same blocks) and also kept the size; the branch is what reports "no block write" and is red on the pre-fix writer in `one_tile_pipeline --selftest`. | VERIFIED (tool, real tile) | H | EXP-2026-11-18-M5.45-idempotence; the 1/2/3-splice block |
| C-4461 | A splice of *different* OSM input over an already-spliced tile is bounded by its own changed blocks, not by the first splice's superseded bytes: on level-2 directory `(76,940)` of `B48R058R` two variants (V1, then V2 with 3 nodes moved ~50 m) go `tile_size 289,319,168 → 289,319,168 → 289,319,168` B, `appended=0` at every step (`in_place=1,1`, then `unchanged=1`), tile SHA-256 `3cd7a3c3…1ba3e` then `a7ae2a36…f6549` for both V2 and its repeat; a full 1,024-parcel level-1 update likewise stays at `293,990,518` B with `superseded_bytes=0` on the repeat. The writer does not re-append `superseded_bytes` of the previous run. | VERIFIED (tool, real tile) | H | EXP-2026-11-18-M5.45-idempotence; the update and level-2 blocks |
| C-4462 | The size consequence is **local to the row**: a directory's slot blocks are disjoint from the directory container. In `B48R058R` the level-1 directory `(76,940)` has `off 161,602,560`, `end 161,619,084` (`span 16,524` B), and its 32 row blocks start at `min block_off = 161,619,200` (factory) / `289,319,168` (after one splice = the factory file size) with `max block_end 163,413,460` (factory) / `293,990,518` (out). So "room to rewrite in place" exists only in the appended region at the end of file, not next to the slot table; a rewrite that changes a block there is an append, and only the identical-block branch avoids it. This is why a same-content rerun adds 0 B while a content change adds the new block once. | VERIFIED (tool, real tile) | H | EXP-2026-11-18-M5.45-idempotence; the block-span census |

## M5.51 — per-range reasons for the metadata a card diff admits (C-4610–C-4619)

byte at FAT0 entry 50,000 and one at FSInfo sector-1 `+0x100` and both were
admitted as "metadata". This pass names every admitted range from the move's
own old/new chains and adds `--strict-metadata`, which refuses any range that
is not one of the move's FAT links or FSInfo words.
